messages.subject: model comparison today
parts:
What's the best practice for comparing models in Stan today, in 1.3? I
know that DIC / WAIC are possibly on the horizon but not there yet. Is
there a way to do cross-validation, perhaps?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] model comparison today
parts:
Today, we've got bupkis (i.e., nothing).

The new edition of "Bayesian Data Analysis" (which is
now complete and going through a final revision) contains
a chapter on the alternatives, including DIC, WAIC
and leave-one-out cross-validation.

There are two coding challenges for Stan.

First, we need to be able to isolate likelihoods (either
for all the data for DIC or item-by-item for WAIC). The
likelihood is not even necessarily specified directly in
a Stan model, much less possible to infer automatically.
For instance, you can write a Stan model using an
analytic posterior without using an expression for the
data likelihood.

Second, we need cross-chain, cross-sample statistics like
sample means to be fed back into the model's likelihood
function.

Cross-validation you can set up on your own from the
outside, but again, if you care about likelihood, you'll
have to write out the likelihood explicitly and save
it as a generated quantity. You can isolate ("cut" in
BUGS terms) the new-data predictions, too, by also putting those
in the generated quantities block. But then you'd have
to run something like RStan, pull out the means, then feed
them back into the model.

We should at least set up an example of how to do this, but
it's never going to be automatic in the same way as BUGS
computes DIC.

- Bob

messages.author: 0839befa8a8b7d53
messages.subject: Re: model comparison today
parts:
As Bob says, you can do DIC yourself, without too much effort. I posted a working script example to this list, months ago. I'll attach it here, as I've updated it since, as the Rstan tools have improved. Note that I use the "textbook" DIC calculation, but there are at least two other popular methods, so worth thinking about that issue some.

My package glmer2stan will compute DIC automatically, but only for standard GLMMs. The package is up on github now: https://github.com/rmcelreath/glmer2stan
